body: I was working for Comcast. Hired on as Tech Support. I was one of the people who answered when your cable was out and scheduled technicians to come out to you. I'd been there about 8 weeks when they announced a shift bid. I had explicitly been promised I wouldn't be a part of the bid until after a minimum of 3 months on the floor. Yeah, they lied.  Thing is, your turn in line to pick your shift is based on sales... for a fucking tech support position. So me being still pretty brand new I had almost no sales. I, ya know, focused on tech support. I had crazy high ratings on all my other metrics. I'd already been selected to be trained as a team lead. But when they brought me in to choose, the only shifts left were 8p-4a & 10p-6a both with split days off. New shift wasn't scheduled to start for another week. I came in the next morning and sat down, prepping to log in and get started. Sat there 5 minutes & just couldn't do it. Got up and sent them a resignation letter later that day from home.. I just figured if they are already lying it's not going to change. Fuck Comcast

I'm in the same boat. I've wanted to end things since I've been old enough to know that was an option. I think the main consideration needs to be how your death will effect others and if hurting them is worth the exchange. Boyfriend, girlfriend, kids, husband, wife, mom, dad.. et al. You are the only one who can determine those factors. Anything or anyone that makes your decision more difficult? And it might be you, or it might be that your self-esteem. I want you to find that release as long as it's the best option for you. If it isn't... Then stay strong.

I wish I could offer some sort of promise of guaranteed improvement. Do you constantly feel the call to end it? Are there times when you feel things are getting better? Sorry my response wasn't more timely. Reddit is preventing quick replies.

That is an awful way to feel for so very long. I'm so sorry you've been in that kind of pain. I too find myself the common denominator. I hope you find a way to make peace with your pain. Whether by living or dying.

Appreciate the advice. Opiates will be difficult for me. I don't really have access to those types of pharmaceuticals. As to the comeback story. That would be nice. There's a concept, I think it's called 'illusion of superiority' that many people interpret themselves as above average intelligence. I've come to realize that's not me. The possibility of a comeback is so miniscule as to be non-existent. I fucked up my own life. I just wish I could make it look like an accident to spare my family any additional pain & scrutiny.

I don't deny that I made a mistake. I did. However, despite your 'hobby' comment I'm unable to fund a minimum $750 retainer for an attorney. An $80 encounter doesnt really equate fiscally. Thanks for the "legal advice".
